short: A pawn with no friendly pawns on either adjacent file.
body: An isolated pawn can never be defended by another pawn, and the square directly in front of it can never be attacked by one. That square is a permanent blockading post for an enemy knight.

It is not simply a weakness. In exchange you get two half-open files for your rooks, more space, and active pieces — which are middlegame assets that disappear when the pieces do. Whether the pawn is a strength or a liability depends entirely on how many pieces are left.

So the two plans are opposites and both are simple. With the isolated pawn: keep pieces on, use the files, attack. Against it: trade pieces, blockade the square in front, and win the pawn in the endgame.

diagram.caption: Black's isolated d5 pawn, and the blockade square in front of it.
